name: Kohima Town
description: Capital of Nagaland and administrative headquarters of Kohima district, a hilly town at about 1444 m elevation known for its ridge-top settlement, markets, and as base for nearby cultural and nature sites.
facts: Lies in Kohima district, Nagaland at approximately 1444 m elevation
Second largest city in the state with Angami Naga cultural influence
Main base for Hornbill Festival and visits to Kisama and Khonoma
Sources: Wikipedia, official district records

name: Kohima War Cemetery
description: Commonwealth War Graves Commission cemetery on Garrison Hill in central Kohima commemorating over 1420 soldiers who died in the 1944 Battle of Kohima, featuring the famous epitaph and preserved tennis court site.
facts: Site of the decisive 1944 Battle of Kohima that halted Japanese advance into India
Contains 1420 Commonwealth burials and memorial to 917 cremated Hindu and Sikh soldiers
Maintained by CWGC; open daily 9am-4pm; epitaph reads 'When you go home tell them of us and say for your tomorrow we gave our today'
Sources: Wikipedia, CWGC official

name: Kisama Heritage Village
description: Naga Heritage Village between Kigwema and Phesama villages, about 12 km south of Kohima, venue of the annual Hornbill Festival with traditional morungs representing Naga tribes.
facts: Name derived from Kigwema and Phesama villages; hosts Hornbill Festival every December
Features traditional tribal houses (morungs) of Naga ethnic groups
Located on NH-2 about 12 km from Kohima
Sources: Wikipedia, kohima.nic.in official

name: Khonoma Green Village
description: Western Angami Naga village about 20 km west of Kohima, India's first green village declared in 2005, known for terraced fields, conservation of Blyth's Tragopan, and historical resistance.
facts: Declared India's first Green Village in 2005 with community ban on hunting
Home to Khonoma Nature Conservation and Tragopan Sanctuary protecting Blyth's Tragopan
Historic site of Angami resistance against British forces in the 19th century
Sources: Wikipedia, official tourism records

name: Dzukou Valley
description: High-altitude alpine valley at about 2450 m near the Nagaland-Manipur border, famous for rolling green hills, dwarf bamboo, seasonal wildflowers, and trekking routes from Viswema and Jakhama.
facts: Accessed primarily from Viswema (gentler route) or Jakhama in Kohima district
Known as Valley of Flowers of the Northeast; best visited for blooms and clear views
Border area with Manipur; permits and local guidance recommended
Sources: Tourism guides, trek reports

name: Japfu Peak
description: Second highest peak in Nagaland at 3048 m in the Barail Range, about 15 km south of Kohima, popular for trekking with views of Dzukou Valley and home to the world's tallest rhododendron tree.
facts: Elevation 3048 m; second highest in Nagaland after Saramati
Holds Guinness record for tallest rhododendron tree
Trek starts from nearby villages like Kigwema; moderate difficulty
Sources: Wikipedia, trek guides

name: Nagaland State Museum
description: State museum on Bayavü Hill in Kohima displaying ethnographic artifacts, tribal costumes, weapons, and cultural items from Naga tribes, established in 1970.
facts: Operated by Department of Art and Culture; opened to public 25 November 1970
Showcases artefacts from across Nagaland's tribes including textiles and sculptures
Located on Upper Bayavü Hill, about 2 km from main town
Sources: Wikipedia, official records

name: Mary Help of Christians Cathedral
description: Catholic cathedral in Kohima noted for architecture blending traditional Naga house elements, with a large carved wooden crucifix; seat of the Diocese of Kohima.
facts: Architecture incorporates traditional Naga house features; 16-foot carved wood crucifix
Consecrated January 1991; construction funded partly by Japanese donors linked to WWII
Seat of the Roman Catholic Diocese of Kohima
Sources: Wikipedia

name: Tuophema Tourist Village
description: Model community-run tourist village about 40 km north of Kohima with traditional Angami Naga cottages representing different khels, offering homestays and cultural immersion.
facts: Established 2001 as community initiative with 12 traditional cottages for different clans
About 40-45 km north of Kohima; known for authentic Naga hospitality and local food
Coordinates approximate; confirm locally
Sources: Nagaland Tourism official, travel guides

name: Dzüleke Village
description: Small Angami Naga eco-tourism village in western Kohima district at about 2130 m, known for community conservation, homestays, streams, and birdlife after hunting ban.
facts: Village council banned hunting in 1999 leading to increased wildlife
Population about 156; elevation around 2130 m; accessed via Khonoma
Community-managed eco-tourism with homestays
Sources: Wikipedia

name: Kachari Ruins (Ruins of Kachari Rajbari)
description: Medieval archaeological site in Dimapur featuring mushroom-domed sandstone pillars and brick ruins from the 10th-13th century Dimasa Kachari kingdom capital, with carved motifs of birds, animals and flowers; protected by ASI.
facts: Ancient capital of Dimasa Kachari kingdom before Ahom conquest
Features distinctive mushroom-shaped pillars 8-15 ft high
Located in central Dimapur opposite Circuit House area
Sources: Wikipedia, dimapur.nic.in official, ASI

name: Dimapur Town
description: Largest city and commercial gateway of Nagaland in Dimapur district, located on the Dhansiri River plains near the Assam border; main air and rail entry point to the state with markets, hotels and base for nearby sites.
facts: Largest city in Nagaland; elevation about 145 m
Only major airport and railway station in the state
Historic Kachari capital area; leased for connectivity in 1963
Sources: Wikipedia, official records

name: Hong Kong Market
description: Bustling flea market in central Dimapur known for affordable imported clothing, footwear, electronics and goods from Myanmar, Thailand and China; popular shopping destination for locals and visitors.
facts: One of the most popular markets in Dimapur for bargains
Grew from Tibetan trader stalls; called state's fashion capital
Located in NST Colony / central area
Sources: Tourism guides, local reports

name: NEZCC Stone Garden and Museum
description: North East Zone Cultural Centre complex near Dimapur Airport featuring a stone sculpture garden with works by Indian artists, traditional morungs, amphitheatre and a museum of Northeast crafts and artifacts.
facts: Headquarters of NEZCC under Ministry of Culture
About 500 m from Dimapur Airport, 3 km from railway station
Showcases Northeast cultural heritage and stone sculptures
Sources: dimapur.nic.in official places-of-interest

name: Nagaland Science Centre
description: Interactive science museum behind Naga Shopping Arcade in Dimapur with galleries on senses, children's exhibits, fun science, planetarium and science park; promotes scientific awareness.
facts: Inaugurated 2004 under Department of Science and Technology
Features interactive exhibits and Tara Mandal planetarium
Near Kachari Ruins; open 10am-4pm except Mondays
Sources: Official records, tourism guides

name: Green Park
description: Recreational park at 4th Mile in Dimapur within the State Horticulture Nursery, offering greenery, boating, adventure activities like zorbing and ziplining, and picnic facilities.
facts: Located at 4th Mile, Dimapur
Includes restaurant, resting shades and water activities
Popular for families and local outings
Sources: dimapur.nic.in official
